purpose: The cross-repo pin for the unaimed-placement lattice: hermes `agent_runtime/office_layout_policy.py` and the launcher's `MissionOfficePlacementPolicy` must resolve every case below to the same slot within 1e-4. Hand-maintained; see README.md for the update rule.

cases.name: empty_floor
cases.why: Nothing placed yet: the first unaimed agent lands on the lattice origin, not on a viewport guess.

cases.name: gap_is_filled_not_appended
cases.why: Columns 0 and 2 taken: the scan fills the HOLE at column 1 rather than appending past the end, which is what makes it deterministic under removal.

cases.name: full_first_row_wraps
cases.why: All eight columns of row 0 taken: the next slot wraps to row 1 column 0 instead of marching off the right edge of the floor.

cases.name: hidden_item_blocks
cases.why: A HIDDEN item still occupies its slot. Hiding is launcher-local view state — hermes has no `hidden` field at all and counts every item it reads — so both sides skip column 0 here, one by honouring the flag and one by never having had it. Un-hiding must never reveal two agents stacked on one point.

cases.name: other_folder_does_not_block
cases.why: A desk sitting on the agent lattice does not push an agent placement: the scan is folder-scoped, and agents sit AT desks.

cases.name: blank_folder_falls_back_to_kind
cases.why: hermes STORES a blank folder (`office_store._safe_folder` returns "" for an absent one) while the launcher's decoder substitutes the kind's default at read time. An item filed under "" is therefore an AGENTS item on one side and would be an unfiled item on the other, so a policy that scanned the raw string would miss this blocker on exactly one of the two repos.

cases.name: blank_folder_desk_falls_back_to_desks
cases.why: The same fallback, the other kind: a blank-foldered DESK belongs to Desks, so it blocks the desk lane and not the agent lattice.

cases.name: desk_lane_offset
cases.why: The desk lane is the agent lattice nudged diagonally by the desk lane offset. Both folders start empty here except for an agent on the agent origin, so without the nudge the first unaimed desk would land exactly under it — the cross-folder stack this policy exists to retire.

cases.name: desk_lane_second_desk
cases.why: A desk already on the lane's origin pushes the next one along the LANE, never back onto the agent lattice.

cases.name: off_lattice_item_blocks_its_nearest_slot
cases.why: A canvas drag lands anywhere. An item 0.14 away from the origin slot blocks it (inside the occupancy radius) and leaves column 1 free (1.30 away, outside it). Neither distance is near the 0.7 boundary, so float32 storage on the launcher side cannot flip the verdict.

cases.name: pigeonhole_200_occupied
cases.why: Twenty-five FULL rows — 200 blockers. The scan is bounded at (occupied + 1) rows, so it terminates, and by pigeonhole a free slot exists inside that bound: row 25, column 0. A policy that stopped scanning at a fixed row count would answer an occupied slot here.
